concept.technique_name: vector addition by resolution into components

examples.problem_statement: Three velocity vectors are given: 10 m/s at 30°, 20 m/s at 90°, and 15 m/s at 195°. Find the resultant velocity vector (magnitude and direction).

solution.operation: Compute horizontal components: For 10 m/s at 30°: $10 \cos 30^\circ = 8.660$ m/s. For 20 m/s at 90°: $20 \cos 90^\circ = 0$ m/s. For 15 m/s at 195°: $15 \cos 195^\circ = -14.489$ m/s.
solution.description: Project each velocity onto the horizontal axis: 10 cos 30 gives 8.660 m/s, 20 cos 90 gives 0, and 15 cos 195 gives minus 14.489 m/s, negative because 195 degrees points to the left.
Add those three horizontal parts. The leftward 14.489 outweighs the rightward 8.660, leaving a horizontal total H of minus 5.829 m/s.

solution.operation: Compute vertical components: For 10 m/s at 30°: $10 \sin 30^\circ = 5$ m/s. For 20 m/s at 90°: $20 \sin 90^\circ = 20$ m/s. For 15 m/s at 195°: $15 \sin 195^\circ = -3.882$ m/s.
solution.description: Now project the same three velocities onto the vertical axis: 10 sin 30 gives 5 m/s, 20 sin 90 gives the full 20 m/s, and 15 sin 195 gives minus 3.882 m/s.
Add the vertical parts to obtain a vertical total V of 21.118 m/s, which is upward since the positive contributions dominate.
H and V are at right angles, so the resultant speed is the square root of H squared plus V squared, which comes to 21.91 m/s.

solution.operation: Direction: $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(V/|H|) = \tan^{-1}(21.118/5.829) = 74.57^\circ$. Since H is negative and V positive, the angle from horizontal is $180^\circ - 74.57^\circ = 105.43^\circ$.
solution.description: Get the reference angle from the sizes alone, the inverse tangent of 21.118 over 5.829, which is 74.57 degrees. A negative H with a positive V is the second quadrant, so the direction from the horizontal is 180 minus 74.57, that is 105.43 degrees.

solution.operation: Calculate horizontal components: $H_1 = 10\cos30° = 8.660$ m/s, $H_2 = 20\cos90° = 0$ m/s, $H_3 = 15\cos195° = -14.489$ m/s
solution.description: Repeat the horizontal resolution in labelled form, writing the three parts as H1, H2 and H3, as a check on the values found in step 1.
Re-add the labelled horizontal parts and confirm the same total as before, minus 5.829 m/s.

solution.operation: Calculate vertical components: $V_1 = 10\sin30° = 5$ m/s, $V_2 = 20\sin90° = 20$ m/s, $V_3 = 15\sin195° = -3.882$ m/s
solution.description: Repeat the vertical resolution with the labels V1, V2 and V3, matching the values found in step 3.
Re-add the labelled vertical parts and confirm the vertical total of 21.118 m/s.
Recompute the magnitude from the confirmed totals; the square root of H squared plus V squared is again 21.91 m/s.
Recompute the reference angle from the magnitudes of the two totals, the inverse tangent of 21.118 over 5.829, again 74.57 degrees.

solution.operation: Adjust angle for quadrant: $\theta = 180° - 74.57° = 105.43°$ from horizontal
solution.description: Apply the same second quadrant adjustment as before, 180 minus 74.57, to state the final direction of 105.43 degrees from the horizontal.

key_reminders: {'point': 'Remember: Vector subtraction can be visualized as adding the negative vector.'}
{'point': 'Caution: When resolving components, ensure correct sign based on quadrant.'}
{'point': 'Speed tip: Use component method for precise calculations when graphical accuracy is limited.'}
common_mistakes: Treating cos 195 degrees as positive, which sends the horizontal total the wrong way and moves the resultant into the wrong quadrant.
Giving the reference angle of 74.57 degrees as the final direction instead of adjusting it to 105.43 degrees.
Rounding the components to one decimal place before summing, which can shift the final angle by more than a degree.
